headline: Adani charts major aviation expansion, ₹2.2 trillion FY27 capex, and bond offerings
summary: Adani Group is seeking government permission to invest in airlines while planning a potential FY28 listing or demerger for its airport business. The conglomerate outlined a ₹2.2 trillion capital expenditure plan for FY27 alongside a $10 billion data centre expansion, as flagship entities prepare public bond issuances.

stories.what: Adani Group has requested Indian government permission to invest in airlines, funds, or backing entrepreneurs launching new carriers. Group CFO Jugeshinder Robbie Singh noted that India's daily flight operations must grow tenfold to 30,000 to serve an untapped pool of 600 million potential passengers.
stories.why: Entering airline investments signals an expansion across the aviation value chain beyond airport ownership, though existing concession rules limit operators from holding over 10% in scheduled carriers to curb conflicts of interest.

brief.happened: Adani Group approached the Indian government seeking approval to invest in existing airlines, dedicated aviation funds, or back new airline entrepreneurs, Group CFO Jugeshinder (Robbie) Singh stated on 27 November 2026. Speaking on the sidelines of the India Debt Capital Market Summit in Mumbai, Singh stated that India operates 3,200 to 3,300 daily flights, but requires nearly 30,000 flights to address demand from 60 crore potential passengers. Singh emphasized the group would prefer acting as an investor while letting entrepreneurs operate the carriers, confirming on-record interest in entering the airline industry.
brief.background: Airport concession agreements in India currently prevent airport operators from owning more than a 10% equity stake in domestic scheduled commercial airlines to avoid conflicts of interest.
brief.next: The group awaits government deliberation regarding regulatory caps governing airport operator ownership in scheduled airlines.

stories.what: Adani Airport Holdings is being structured for a potential demerger or initial public offering in FY28, with its internal corporate setup slated for completion next year. The arm is increasing its non-aeronautical revenue contribution from 60% toward 65% or higher.
stories.why: Preparing the airport vertical for independent capital generation ensures the infrastructure arm can self-fund future investment cycles without reliance on group balance sheets.

brief.happened: The Adani Group is preparing the ground to list its airport division, targeting an initial public offering or corporate demerger by FY28, Group CFO Jugeshinder Singh said in Mumbai on 27 November 2026. Singh noted that the business's corporate structure will be ready next year to ensure the business can independently fund its ongoing investment programme. Non-aeronautical revenue currently accounts for approximately 60% of Adani's airport business revenues, and management expects this proportion to expand to 65% or more over time.
brief.background: Adani Group operates eight airports across India and plans a broader $140 billion capital expenditure program across group companies over five years.
brief.next: Completion of Adani Airport Holdings' structural preparation in 2027 ahead of listing steps in FY28.

stories.what: Adani Group projected capital expenditure of ₹2.2 lakh crore ($23.72 billion) for FY27 alongside plans to invest up to $10 billion in data centres over the next four years. Annual group borrowings are estimated at ₹1.3 lakh crore to ₹1.4 lakh crore across FY27 and FY28.
stories.why: The figures lay bare the conglomerate's scale of ongoing leverage and expansion, showing that flagship infrastructure ventures continue to rely on heavy debt financing.

brief.happened: Adani Group plans ₹2.2 trillion (around $23.72 billion) in capital expenditure for FY27, Group CFO Robbie Singh announced at the India Debt Capital Market Summit 2026 on 27 November. Singh projected annual borrowings of ₹1.3 to ₹1.4 lakh crore each in FY27 and FY28 from domestic and global credit markets. Concurrently, the conglomerate intends to deploy up to $10 billion over four years into digital infrastructure through AdaniConneX, its data centre joint venture with EdgeConneX supported by group renewable power.
brief.background: The group's digital infrastructure platform operates via AdaniConneX, a 50-50 joint venture between Adani Enterprises and EdgeConneX powered by renewable supply from group entities.
brief.next: Syndication and debt raising across domestic and international bond markets starting early 2027.

stories.what: Adani Enterprises and Adani Power are preparing public bond sales in India to raise at least ₹20 billion ($220 million). Flagship Adani Enterprises is targeting ₹10 billion to ₹20 billion with an issuance expected in early December 2026.
stories.why: Tapping local public retail and institutional bond markets diversifies funding sources away from foreign credit lines and private institutional placements.

brief.happened: Adani Enterprises and Adani Power are preparing public bond offerings targeting at least ₹20 billion ($220 million), sources reported on 26 November 2026. Merchant bankers indicated that Adani Enterprises aims to raise between ₹10 billion and ₹20 billion through a public issue planned to launch in the first half of December. The issues represent key domestic capital generation steps as the conglomerate taps wider pools of Indian onshore liquidity to support growth.
brief.background: The planned issuances would be among the prominent public debt offerings by the flagship units in the onshore domestic bond market.
brief.next: Filing of bond prospectus with domestic stock exchanges and debt regulators ahead of December launch.

stories.what: Adani Energy Solutions Limited awarded two purchase orders to Diamond Power Infrastructure for the supply of AL-59 conductors. The conductors are earmarked for the Bhadla-Fatehpur ±800 kV high-voltage direct current transmission corridor.
stories.why: Procurement of critical transmission conductors reflects continued equipment execution on key inter-state green power evacuation corridors.

brief.happened: Adani Energy Solutions Limited awarded two procurement contracts on 25 November 2026 to Diamond Power Infrastructure Limited. The orders mandate the supply of AL-59 grade conductors for the Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh sections of the Bhadla-Fatehpur ±800 kV high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission link, resulting in Diamond Power's stock gaining 2% on 26 November.
brief.background: The Bhadla-Fatehpur HVDC transmission line is designed to evacuate bulk renewable power generated in Western India into Northern load centres.

concept.explain: Non-aeronautical revenue refers to income an airport operator generates outside core aviation services like aircraft landing and parking fees. It includes duty-free sales, retail, food and beverage concessions, car parking, and real estate leasing within terminals. For airport operators, expanding this stream from 60% to over 65% stabilizes operating cash flow because retail and concession margins are unregulated and provide higher yields than aeronautical tariffs set by regulators.

question.q: Why is the Adani Group seeking regulatory clearance to invest in airlines instead of operating one directly, and what is the strategic hurdle?
question.a: Concession agreements bar airport operators from owning more than 10% in scheduled domestic carriers to prevent anti-competitive behaviour and conflict of interest. Adani wants clearance to back entrepreneurs or invest passively, stimulating domestic flight volume from 3,300 toward 30,000 daily flights to fill capacity across its eight airports without taking on operational carrier liabilities.

script: Good morning, Aashish. Here is your Adani briefing for Saturday, 28 November. We start today with major strategic announcements unveiled by Group Chief Financial Officer Jugeshinder Robbie Singh at the India Debt Capital Market Summit in Mumbai. First, Adani Group has formally approached the government seeking regulatory approval to invest in domestic airlines. India currently caps an airport operator's stake in scheduled commercial airlines at 10 percent to prevent conflicts of interest. The group is requesting permission to invest in airlines, launch aviation funds, or back entrepreneurs. Singh highlighted that while India currently operates roughly 3,300 daily flights, the market has over 60 crore potential passengers requiring nearly 30,000 daily flights. Singh emphasized the group prefers acting as a financial backer while letting professional entrepreneurs operate the carriers. Second, the group outlined listing plans for Adani Airport Holdings Limited. The corporate structural groundwork is expected to conclude next year, setting the stage for a demerger or an initial public offering in fiscal year 2028. Management noted that non-aeronautical revenue currently makes up about 60 percent of the airport business and is targeted to reach 65 percent or higher, enabling the business to self-fund its investments. Third, on group capital allocation, Adani is planning a massive 2.2 lakh crore rupee capital expenditure programme in fiscal year 2027. Group entities expect total borrowings of 1.3 to 1.4 lakh crore rupees annually across both fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028. Additionally, the group plans to invest up to 10 billion dollars in data centres over four years through AdaniConneX, its joint venture with EdgeConneX. Turning to immediate domestic financing, flagship Adani Enterprises and Adani Power are preparing public bond issuances in India to raise at least 20 billion rupees, equivalent to 220 million dollars. Adani Enterprises is eyeing between 10 and 20 billion rupees, with merchant bankers indicating an issue launch in the first half of December. In the utilities and transmission space, Adani Energy Solutions Limited, AESL, has awarded two procurement contracts to Diamond Power Infrastructure. The purchase orders cover the supply of AL-59 conductors for the Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh stretches of the ±800 kV Bhadla to Fatehpur high-voltage direct current line, driving a 2 percent gain in the supplier's shares. Over in Gujarat, Adani Green Energy Limited's 538-square-kilometre hybrid facility at Khavda received public attention following a visit by music artist Diljit Dosanjh, who toured the installation and lauded the site engineers stationed in the remote salt desert. At the state level, the Andhra Pradesh cabinet has officially approved a 13,667 crore rupee investment proposal submitted by the Adani Group alongside an expansion by automaker Kia. Finally, Chairman Gautam Adani visited the Mumbai Book Festival at Mumbai University's Kalina campus, engaging with young students and encouraging reading habits. Our business concept of the day is Non-Aeronautical Revenue. These are commercial earnings generated at airports from shopping, dining, and parking rather than airline takeoff or landing fees. Because these earnings are unregulated, lifting them past 65 percent dramatically boosts margins and stability ahead of the planned 2028 airport listing. Here is a sharp question to consider today: If the government relaxes the 10 percent concession ownership cap, what structural advantages does an airport operator gain from holding passive stakes in scheduled airlines? Have a productive day ahead.
